clue.text: According to Spooner, conveniences for pets are symbols of the working class

indicators.note: Spooner swapped the opening sounds of words, so the phrase defined next must have its initial sounds exchanged

blocks.note: small hinged doors that let a cat come and go; swapping the first sounds of the two words gives the answer

explanation.surface: A sociologist decides that pet doors mark a household as working class.
explanation.walkthrough: Cat flaps, swapped, become FLAT CAPS: the cloth caps long associated with British working men.
explanation.definitionFit: The cloth cap is a traditional emblem of British manual labourers, pigeon fanciers and northern industrial towns.

clue.text: Believer during Ramadan getting more resolute

blocks.note: first meaning: a Muslim who abstains from food in daylight hours that month
second meaning: firmer, more fixed, as in held more securely

explanation.surface: A devout Muslim growing more determined through the holy month.
explanation.definitionFit: One who fasts abstains from food, and fast as an adjective also means firmly fixed, so its comparative is firmer.

clue.text: Primarily, ancient Royal Marines’ adversaries Drake annihilated?

definitions.text: Primarily, ancient Royal Marines’ adversaries Drake annihilated?

indicators.note: primarily means in the first place, so only the opening letter of each word counts

blocks.clueFragment: ancient Royal Marines’ adversaries Drake annihilated
blocks.note: the initial letters of the six words

explanation.surface: A history lesson on the old foes of English sailors that Sir Francis Drake routed.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition too: Drake helped defeat the Spanish fleet in 1588.
explanation.definitionFit: The Spanish fleet of 1588 sailed against England and was scattered by English ships and storms.

clue.text: Between mountain pass and narrow elevation, English versifier

indicators.note: between places one letter in the gap separating the two clued words

blocks.note: a col is a low pass between peaks
E is the abbreviation for English
a ridge is a long narrow raised strip of land

explanation.surface: A poet located somewhere among mountain passes and ridges, like a Lake District walker.
explanation.walkthrough: Samuel Taylor Coleridge wrote The Rime of the Ancient Mariner and walked the Lake District fells.
explanation.definitionFit: A Romantic poet, so a writer of verse, which is exactly what the word means.

clue.text: Corpulent sags I cut up!

indicators.note: something cut up is chopped and rearranged, so the preceding letters are reordered

blocks.note: the fourteen letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A cosmetic doctor announces cutting into sagging flesh.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: the speaker who cuts up fat and sagging skin.
explanation.definitionFit: A cosmetic doctor operates to reshape bodies, removing fat and tightening loose skin with a scalpel.

clue.text: Church music: where to be seated

blocks.note: CH is the standard abbreviation for church
an air is a tune or melody

explanation.surface: A notice in a church about the music, then directions to the seats.
explanation.definitionFit: A seat is a piece of furniture for sitting on, so the noun names somewhere a person sits down.

clue.text: Junk food firm

blocks.note: first meaning: a thin fried potato slice sold in bags, which Americans call a chip
second meaning: pleasantly hard and fresh, as of an apple or lettuce

explanation.surface: A company that makes unhealthy snacks.
explanation.definitionFit: In Britain the bagged potato snack has this name, and the adjective describes something brittle, fresh and hard.

clue.text: What can be seen in book of maps? Not this island, for starters!

definitions.text: What can be seen in book of maps? Not this island, for starters!

indicators.note: starters are opening items, so only the initial letter of each of the three words is kept
something seen in a book sits inside it, so the kept letters go inside the volume's name

blocks.note: an atlas is a bound collection of maps
the opening letters of the three words

explanation.surface: A riddle about the one island no map book will show.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition too: a legendary island is the one place an atlas cannot show.
explanation.definitionFit: Plato's sunken island is mythical, so it appears on no real map of the world.

clue.text: Filthy location left amid tall grass given new appearance

indicators.note: amid means in the middle of, so the earlier pieces go inside the plant word

blocks.note: a reed is a tall grass of wet ground
a pigsty is a byword for a dirty place
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: A pigsty abandoned in long grass gets a makeover.
explanation.definitionFit: To restyle something is to redesign how it looks, so it has been given a different look.

clue.text: Countries getting along swimmingly? She might not agree

indicators.note: swimming letters move about freely, so the phrase before is rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Nations in harmony, with one sceptic dissenting.
explanation.walkthrough: Nicola Sturgeon led the Scottish National Party, which campaigns for Scotland to leave the UK; 'swimmingly' also nods to the fish in her surname.
explanation.definitionFit: As Scotland's former First Minister pushing independence, she would dispute that the UK's nations rub along happily together.

clue.text: So, an African country, a nation of Africa

blocks.note: taken as written
Mali is a landlocked West African state
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone listing African states one after another.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue names two African countries: the wordplay one is MALI, the defined one the whole answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Somalia is a state in the Horn of Africa, on the continent's eastern coast.

clue.text: What's caused by cold weather? I see, I see: son’s skipping lesson

indicators.note: to skip something is to leave it out, so the named small word is dropped from the longer one

blocks.note: each 'I see' is I plus C, the letter that sounds like 'see'
taken as written
taken as written, the part removed

explanation.surface: A teacher grasps why a pupil is absent: the son is missing a lesson in the cold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I see' is the letter I plus C, which sounds like 'see', and the clue says it twice.
explanation.definitionFit: Hanging spikes of ice form when dripping water freezes, which happens in freezing winter conditions.

clue.text: Respected figure among midfielders

indicators.note: among says the letters sit inside the following word rather than being clued by its meaning

blocks.note: the letters run inside the word, from its fifth to ninth

explanation.surface: A senior, respected player in a football team's midfield.
explanation.definitionFit: An older person whose experience earns authority and deference in a community or church.

clue.text: A pony went bananas: that's seen all the time

indicators.note: going bananas is going crazy, so the letters before it are thrown into disorder

blocks.note: taken as written
the word itself joins the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A pony running wild is described as a common sight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Went' does double duty in the surface but its letters are part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Something available everywhere and cheaply is so common it has little value, which the idiom expresses.

clue.text: Use your wits: plunge into water and plunge into water

blocks.note: to duck someone is to push them under water
taken as written
to dive is to jump head first into water

explanation.surface: Survival advice for a swimmer that just repeats itself.
explanation.walkthrough: The repeated phrase is clued two ways, a push under and a headlong jump.
explanation.definitionFit: The British idiom means getting by through evasion, improvisation and dodging trouble cleverly.

clue.text: Fly south, taking minutes, not seconds, to coastal town

indicators.note: taking brings one letter in, and the following not says which letter it replaces

blocks.note: to dart is to move swiftly, to fly
taken as written
M is the abbreviation for minutes
S is the abbreviation for seconds

explanation.surface: Instructions for a quick trip south to the seaside.
explanation.walkthrough: In SOUTH the S gives way to M, making MOUTH. Dartmouth is a Devon port, home of the Royal Navy's officer college.
explanation.definitionFit: The Devon harbour sits at the river Dart's estuary on England's south coast.

clue.text: A model? The Observer is, in a way

blocks.note: taken as written
to model for an artist is to sit for them
a newspaper speaks of itself as 'we', so the paper is says 'we are', contracted

explanation.surface: Is the Observer newspaper a model to follow? Sort of.
explanation.walkthrough: The Observer is a British Sunday paper; editorials use 'we', so 'The Observer is' becomes we're, written without the apostrophe.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase hedges a statement, meaning so to speak or in a manner of speaking.

clue.text: Type of movie where star dies surprisingly?

indicators.note: surprisingly hints at an unexpected outcome, so the letters come out in an unexpected order

blocks.note: the eight letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A film genre where the lead actor unexpectedly gets killed off.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also hints at the answer: a star dying unexpectedly would be a calamity for a film.
explanation.definitionFit: The genre of catastrophe films about earthquakes, sinking ships or burning towers takes its name from the word.

clue.text: Trail guides displayed technique with axe

indicators.note: displayed suggests spread out and laid open in a new layout, so the preceding letters are set out afresh

blocks.note: the eleven letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Mountain guides showing off their skill at chopping wood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Axe' looks like a woodcutter's tool, but it is slang for a guitar.
explanation.definitionFit: A player glides a metal or glass tube along the strings of the instrument, a playing method of blues musicians.

clue.text: City, European, very pleasant to go around?

indicators.note: going around something encloses it, so the next words' letters wrap the single letter

blocks.note: V is the abbreviation for very
E is the abbreviation for European
nice means agreeable

explanation.surface: A traveller asks whether a European city is pleasant to tour.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian lagoon city is famous for canals, gondolas and its Grand Canal.

clue.text: Wasted, stoned in European city

indicators.note: wasted describes something ruined or in a mess, so the next word's letters are scrambled

blocks.note: the six letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A drunk or drugged tourist on a weekend away abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wasted' and 'stoned' both read as intoxicated, but only one supplies letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Ostend is a Belgian port and seaside resort on the North Sea coast.

clue.text: To ridicule the French, Trump recalled battle they lost

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so the whole string so far is read in the opposite direction

blocks.note: to rag someone is to tease or mock them
la is a French word for 'the'
in British slang to trump is to break wind

explanation.surface: A jibe at the French with a nod to a president remembering their defeat.
explanation.walkthrough: Trump is not the politician but British slang for breaking wind; 'they' points back to the French.
explanation.definitionFit: Nelson defeated the French and Spanish fleets off Cape Trafalgar in 1805, so the name fits a French defeat.

clue.text: Unionist soldiers surrounding female family members

indicators.note: surrounding means enclosing, so the insects' letters close around the single one

blocks.note: soldier ants are a caste of the insect
U is the abbreviation for Unionist

explanation.surface: Union troops guarding the women of a family, like a Civil War scene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Soldiers' suggests troops, but here they are insects.
explanation.definitionFit: A parent's sisters are relatives, women who belong to the wider family.

clue.text: NY sportsmen filled with energy for fixtures

indicators.note: a team filled with something holds it inside, so one letter goes within the team name

blocks.note: the New York Mets are a baseball team
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: New York athletes full of energy for their scheduled games.
explanation.definitionFit: Sporting fixtures are scheduled contests, and a meet is an organised athletics or racing event.

clue.text: Consume some buckwheat in tortilla

indicators.note: some means only part of the following words is used, a run of their letters

blocks.note: the letters run across the three words, from inside the first to the start of the last

explanation.surface: A diner eating buckwheat wrapped in a tortilla.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means to use up or erode something gradually, as savings are consumed by bills.

clue.text: Hastily ‘reunited’ with North excluded – very clever

indicators.note: things done hastily come out jumbled, so the quoted word is rearranged
excluded means left out, so the compass letter is removed first

blocks.note: taken as written
N is the compass abbreviation for north, the letter removed

explanation.surface: A hurried reunion leaves out someone from the north, which is thought very smart.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone learned has deep scholarly knowledge, so the adjective suits a highly intelligent, well-read person.

clue.text: Neuroses involving money

indicators.note: involving says the word contains the letters wanted, rather than defining them

blocks.note: the letters run from the second to the sixth of the word

explanation.surface: Anxieties that revolve around finances.
explanation.definitionFit: The currency of most European Union countries, so plural units of cash.

clue.text: In Yorkshire you will enter hostelry, with a little drink sooner or later

indicators.note: to enter is to go inside, so the dialect pronoun goes into the inn word
a little of a word is just its first letter

blocks.note: an inn is a pub or small hotel
thee survives as the word for 'you' in Yorkshire dialect
the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: A Yorkshire invitation into the pub for a small drink, eventually.
explanation.walkthrough: Yorkshire is an English county whose dialect still uses old forms like thee for 'you'.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means eventually, after everything has been considered or once time has passed.
